nodes_add.note: Family background of Meher Baba; Zoroaster is the first of the six earlier Avatars in his scheme.

nodes_add.name: Sufism Reoriented
nodes_add.note: California Sufi group accepted Meher Baba as its leader and renamed by him in 1952; publishes God Speaks and God in a Pill?

nodes_add.name: Pete Townshend
nodes_add.note: Guitarist of The Who; heard of Meher Baba from Mike McInnerney in autumn 1967 (his account, Rolling Stone 1970); dedicated Tommy (1969) to him.

nodes_update.name: Meher Baba
nodes_update.note: Merwan Sheriar Irani, b. 25 Feb 1894 Pune; silent from 10 July 1925; first publicly declared himself the Avatar Feb 1954 (Trust brief biography); Meher Baba's Call issued 12 Sept 1954 at a mass darshan in Ahmednagar; Final Declaration 30 Sept 1954 at Meherabad; d. 31 Jan 1969 Meherazad, entombed at Meherabad.

nodes_update.name: Hazrat Babajan
nodes_update.note: Pashtun faqir of Pune; birth estimates c. 1790-1820; d. 21 Sept 1931 Pune; kiss on Merwan's forehead dated May 1913 (embrace) / Jan 1914 (kiss) in Trust chronology.

nodes_update.name: Tajuddin Baba
nodes_update.note: Nagpur saint; b. 17 or 27 Jan 1861 depending on source; d. 17 Aug 1925.

nodes_update.name: Narayan Maharaj
nodes_update.note: Of Kedgaon; b. 20 May 1885, d. 3 Sept 1945 per Wikipedia; birthplace given as Nargund or Bagalkot.

edges_upsert.note: Embrace May 1913 and kiss January 1914 per Trust chronology; event rests on Baba's own account and devotee biographies. Babajan herself is independently attested as a Pune faqir with a dargah.

First contact Dec 1915 at Khandoba's temple, Shirdi (Trust chronology); repeated visits from 1916, at Shirdi then Sakori (from 1917); Upasni praised him publicly in late 1921 (Purdom, via Wikipedia); last meeting 17 Oct 1941 at Dahigaon.

Single meeting, December 1915 (Trust chronology). Shri Sai Satcharita does not mention Meher Baba (Wikipedia). The 'Parvardigar' greeting is told in devotee biographies with no independent witness (hagiographic).
One visit at Nagpur/Waki, April 1915 (Trust chronology); Baba's account.
One visit at Kedgaon, April 1915, returned within 24 hours (Trust chronology); Baba's account.
Qutub, mast, fana vocabulary; Babajan a Muslim faqir. Scholars (Sedgwick, per Wikipedia) see few similarities with the Sufi Movement beyond universalism.
Born to Zoroastrian parents; lists Zoroaster as the first earlier Avatar. Not a teacher of Zoroastrian doctrine (Shepherd).
Accepted as leader of a California Sufi group; renamed Sufism Reoriented in 1952.
Heard of Baba autumn 1967 (Townshend, Rolling Stone 1970); dedicated Tommy (1969) to him.

glossary.def: "Descent." In Hindu usage, God taking human form. Meher Baba used it for the one soul he said returns every 700 to 1,400 years, and said he was the Avatar of his age.
In Meher Baba's teaching, one of the five God-realised souls who at any time hold the office of guiding the world; the same role as a sadguru or qutub.
A true teacher who has himself realised God.
In Sufism, the spiritual 'pole' of an age, the saint on whom the order of the world is said to rest.
A word Meher Baba took from the Sufi phrase for one intoxicated with God. A mast may look mad to others because of absorption in inner experience.
The circle of close disciples who lived and worked with Meher Baba, and who voiced his gestures after 1954.
"Close company." The time devotees spend living near Meher Baba, used for the retreats he held with followers.
An impression left in the mind by experience. In God Speaks, the impressions that build up as a soul passes through forms and bind it to the sense of being separate.

issues: meher-baba.mdx: the date of the Avatar declaration is unresolved. The Trust's brief biography and meherabode.org say February 1954 and the New World Encyclopedia says 10 February 1954; the Trust-related chronology (meherabode.org/1950s) and Wikipedia give Meher Baba's Call as 12 Sept 1954 and the Final Declaration as 30 Sept 1954 at Meherabad. The chapter gives both. The writer could not locate the full texts.

meher-baba.mdx: Babajan encounter dated May 1913 (embrace) and January 1914 (kiss) in the Trust chronology and Wikipedia's Babajan article; Wikipedia's Meher Baba article implies 1913. The chapter gives the range. Her age at death is unknowable (birth estimates c. 1790-1820).
meher-baba.mdx: alphabet board start is 7 Jan 1927 in the Trust chronology (also writing stopped 2 Jan 1927), but Wikipedia says last written message 1 Dec 1926. Trust bio says 1927. Chapter hedges.
meher-baba.mdx: place of death. Trust pages say Meherazad; Wikipedia's text says Meherabad (buried there). Chapter uses Meherazad.

meher-baba.mdx: 'Don't worry, be happy' attribution. Wikipedia, Meher Mount and IPKat say Baba used the phrase with Western followers and it appeared on 1960s posters, but no page checked gives his exact wording, date or addressee. The Meher Mount page quotes a different line to a nurse (Always say, 'All is well and beautiful. I will be happy.'), cited to Lord Meher. The McFerrin/Tuck and Patti poster story is 'citation needed' on Wikipedia. McFerrin's 1988 USA Weekend remark is seen only second-hand via IPKat. Author may want to locate the Lord Meher passage or a dated cable.

meher-baba.mdx: quotations were taken from WebFetch summaries (curl to source sites was blocked). The following should be re-checked verbatim against the originals by the fact-checker: 'a limitation that He assumed for the spiritual upliftment of humanity' (Trust brief bio), 'complete helplessness and hopelessness in total reliance on God' (Trust), 'irrespective of the doubts and convictions', 'If God can be found through the medium of any drug, God is not worthy of being God', 'During the Avataric period, the five Perfect Masters make God incarnate as man', the Awakener quotations from the 13 Nov 1954 notes, 'Do not forget that I am God', and McFerrin's USA Weekend remark. The God Speaks quotation 'ALL souls (atmas) were, are and will be in the Over-Soul (Paramatma)' came from the Trust PDF's opening of Part 1.

meher-baba.mdx: the full text of Meher Baba's Call and Final Declaration was not found; only fragments in The Awakener. The 'stabbed in the back' prediction is quoted from the 13 Nov 1954 Satara notes, not from the declaration itself. Devotee interpretation of these predictions was not found beyond the Trust calling them 'enigmatic'.

meher-baba.mdx: the God Speaks cosmology section relies on the Trust PDF's contents and first 16 pages, plus Wikipedia's summary for the kingdoms and planes. The fetch did not reach Parts 3-9, so details of the fourth plane, reincarnation and the seven planes are stated only at the level Wikipedia and the Trust biography support. Wikipedia lists stone, metal, vegetable, worm, fish, bird, animal, then human.

meher-baba.mdx: Narayan Maharaj birthplace and samadhi location are inconsistent on Wikipedia (Nargund vs Bagalkot; died Bangalore). Chapter gives only dates and Kedgaon. Tajuddin birth date 17 Jan 1861 (Aiyer 1973 devotional text) vs 27 Jan (Wikipedia); chapter says 17 or 27.

meher-baba.mdx: legal controversies. No charge, conviction or judgement against Meher Baba was found. Wikipedia says Upasni's Kanya Kumari Sthan drew public criticism and legal cases in which he was acquitted on appeal; this was not verified and is left to Upasni's entry. No dispute over the Meher Baba Trust's registration was found in the sources reviewed.

meher-baba.mdx: Shepherd's critical commentary page was read only in summary; the claim that he treats the three (Sai Baba, Upasni, Meher Baba) as separate movements, and his critique of Lord Meher, should be checked against his own texts (Gurus Rediscovered 1986; Hazrat Babajan 2014; Lord Meher Critique 2017).

meher-baba.mdx: the Brunton claim ('disillusioned account') is from Wikipedia and New World Encyclopedia only; Brunton's chapter 'I Meet a Messiah' was not read. His book is on archive.org if the author wants a direct quote.

meher-baba.mdx: no direct video URL was found for the 1932 newsreel or the 1967 Beyond Words footage; media cards flag this. The USC link is a catalogue record. avatarmeherbaba.org/media.html and Meher Film Works (meherfilmworks.org) were seen in search results but not fetched.
meher-baba.mdx: places coordinates marked verified:false are approximate; the existing places.json already has Meherabad (19.05, 74.78) and Pune. Confirm Sakori, Meherazad and the two US centres.
meher-baba.mdx: glossary 'Qutub' uses lang ur with Arabic script; change to ar if the site prefers. Sahavas definition is the writer's gloss from Trust usage; no glossary source page fetched.
meher-baba.mdx: frontmatter has no titleScript. The title 'The Word of Words' is taken from the 13 Nov 1954 notes in The Awakener.

Graph: existing edges upasni-maharaj to meher-baba and shirdi-sai-baba to meher-baba are upserted and re-graded; Babajan, Tajuddin and Narayan edges changed from influenced/documented to claimed/testimony. The author may prefer to keep 'influenced' for the type.

meher-baba.mdx (factcheck): Hollywood silence-breaking date conflict. The Los Angeles Times (30 May 1932, via Calisphere) reported he would break silence in Hollywood on 13 July 1932; Wikipedia and meherabode.org/1930s place the Hollywood Bowl announcement and abrupt sailing to Hong Kong in 1934. Chapter gives both; author may wish to check Lord Meher.

meher-baba.mdx (factcheck): Meherazad coordinates moved from 19.06,74.75 (which is south of Ahmednagar, near Meherabad) to approx. 19.16,74.73 (north of the city, near Pimpalgaon Malwa); still unverified. Also 'residence from 1952' in the place note was changed to 'approx. 1949'; confirm.
